author: ToxicNinja
quote:
This is a game that came out 15 years too late.

I have a special place in my heart for world of goo. In the dark ages of indie gaming, many years before Terraria, FTL, or even minecraft, all indie games on pc were exclusively ports from the iphone 2-3, mindless gamblecore tier nonsense like peggle was the peak. When this game originally came out it sold developers on the idea that a small group of developers could take a simple concept and make an amazing game. In 2008 this was effectively seen as a novelty, a one-off in an industry driven exclusively by AAA developers pushing multi million dollar budgets. The problem is it's not 2008 anymore. This exact game would have been a 10/10 in 2009, maybe 2010, but waiting 16 years for a game that at best feels like a soft remake? The industry has changed a lot since the original came out. 90% of games are made by small teams with small budgets, and AAA have become overfitted in their own slop of regurgitated failure aside from the occasional passion project like cyberpunk or bg3. I feel like the worst crime this game commits is against its legacy. Where once it was on the forefront of a concept of small scale development this sequel feels like EA bought it, rebranded it, and we're 12 sequels deep in a regurgitated ocean. The game makes this joke with the detective bits but it feels like it goes past parody and just becomes exactly what it's complaining about.
Overall a mundane experience, not much in the way of new ideas or clever innovation, just an unreleased dlc someone found from a bygone era.

author: ToxicNinja
quote:
The depth and scale of a desert after rain.

I've played every Bethesda game since daggerfall each around when they came out, I'm not a big Bethesda fan I'm just old, and Bethesda games despite never being perfect always manage to string together some unique mechanics, interesting stories, and engaging gameplay that guarantee I'm going to get my money's worth even if they're a little rough around the edges. They've had their ups and downs, and the only thing I generally find abjectly annoying is the general oversimplication their games are facing with each iteration, but despite which fallout 4 and skyrim were still games I greatly enjoyed.

This is where the problems with starfield start. This "game" is not really a "game", it's a hodgepodge of video game mechanics strung together. It has an xp system, it has killing, it has ammo and guns, and it has plots, but at no point do any of these individual systems seem to mesh together to make a functional video games, each mechanic seems like it's fighting for center stage. I spent most of my time trying to make a functional series of linked habitats, the general problems here were; it takes a lot of levels to build on planets with mandatory resources to get the wheels spinning. There was really no value in any of this as the weapon upgrades weren't worth a 15+ level grind, and the level scaling makes the upgrades negligible at best. Storage was always a problem, and shipping goods between planets is a chore at best. Thus I had no fun building a settlement, and it was completely detached from the "game" as it did nothing to progress quests or make my life in starfield easier or more fulfilling. All of the quests I did were equally uninspired and consisted of the usual "go here, talk to person, kill raiders" loop, as with every "random" encounters generated on the "random" planets lacking any sort of personality or purpose. The quest rewards were mostly pointless and I stopped doing quests when I realized the pathetic amount of XP they were giving. The main story is probably the most audacious waste of time as there usually isn't even anything to fight, it's more of a sight-seeing trip with a terrible floating-around minigame. The only memories I made in this game were lugging around garbage, only to drop it off somewhere, only to spend 30 minutes sorting garbage because all my garbage storage is full, only to realize I didn't pick up the one vial of plutonic gooblegok which I need to finish this upgrade so now I have to go back to the planet, watching 6 loading screens in the process.

I do have 2 pluses;
1. The physics system is really good, especially for a bethesda game.
2. The detail on the misc garbage items is really 10/10.

Overall I feel like this game was built with zero team cohesion, probably a bunch of board room meetings filled with people who have never played a video game in their life that wasn't on an iphone created this game, who then gave terrible instructions to programmers and artists who thought they were making a game that could be fun but when they realized none of the subcomponents they made worked together they shipped it anyway and said "modders will fix it, and we'll take a cut."
